sn36.4:1.1: “Bhikkhus, when the uninstructed worldling makes the statement,
sn36.4:1.2: ‘In the great ocean there is a bottomless abyss,’
sn36.4:1.3: he makes such a statement about something that is nonexistent and unreal.
sn36.4:1.5: This, bhikkhus, is rather a designation for painful bodily feelings, that is, ‘bottomless abyss.’
sn36.4:1.6: “When the uninstructed worldling is contacted by a painful bodily feeling, he sorrows, grieves, and laments; he weeps and beats his breast and becomes distraught.
sn36.4:1.7: This is called an uninstructed worldling who has not risen up in the bottomless abyss, one who has not gained a foothold.
sn36.4:1.8: “But, bhikkhus, when the instructed noble disciple is contacted by a painful bodily feeling, he does not sorrow, grieve, or lament; he does not weep and beat his breast and become distraught.
sn36.4:1.9: This is called an instructed noble disciple who has risen up in the bottomless abyss, one who has gained a foothold.”
sn36.4:2.3: Bodily feelings that sap one’s life,
sn36.4:2.4: Who trembles when they touch him,
sn36.4:3.2: Who weeps out loud and wails:
sn36.4:3.3: He has not risen up in the bottomless abyss,
sn36.4:3.4: Nor has he even gained a foothold.
sn36.4:4.1: But one who is able to endure them—
sn36.4:4.3: Bodily feelings that sap one’s life—
sn36.4:4.4: Who trembles not when they touch him:
sn36.4:4.5: He has risen up in the bottomless abyss,
sn36.4:4.6: And he has also gained a foothold.
